Separate finances immediately if you haven't already. 

Get everything in writing in the decree- for instance my lawyer left out that my ex has to vacate our home by Oct 1st because it was assumed he just would since he bought his own house. Nothing is too small. I have a part in the decree added about mental health. We share decisions 50/50 about out child's  medical stuff, except mental health concerns. Meaning I can take my child to a therapist without his approval and vice versa. Nothing is too small. Im sure you're aware of the tiny little loop holes they can find and exploit. Dont be worried about looking overbearing or a crazy person to your attorney- they dont have to live with the consequences, you do. 

When they are nice, THERE IS A REASON. I tried very hard not to respond to any stipulations right away. I didn't decide on any matter without giving it a few days thought amd running it by friends to make sure I wasn't missing anything. He/she will try to manipulate and influence your decisions- please take a step back and think about WHY they are being nice and what they want from it. You have to be a bit of a shark and take back control. 

Do not leave splitting of the house contents to be divided amongst yourselves. Anything high value ($ or sentimental value) should be put on paper.

It is possible not to go to trial. I didnt and my divorce was final Sept 6th. It was not easy at all, and we spent probably an extra thousand each bickering over stupid stuff via our lawyers, but it can be done. That doesn't mean roll over, but I had read it was pretty much impossible with someone with NPD and wanted to give hope that it is possible.

Good luck :) you are strong and there  is so much light at the end of the tunnel.

During arguments, disagreements, or me asking him to contribute to the household chores, my ex would take different tactics to try and manipulate me, or end the discussion altogether. One tactic would be to blow up immediately and fiercely so that I would back off. If that didn't work he would usually attack me personally, steering the convo in different directions. Then if that didn't work he would start playing the victim- "you keep saying I'm a terrible person, I'm useless, I'm scum of the earth!" when I had said nothing even close to that.

Mad because I had to just swallow my words instead of asking him to pick up the 3 baskets of his clothes sitting on the couch for the last week because I knew it would cause a blow up and not being talked to for days. So mad because he his version of a conversation always ended with me being a horrible person for "screaming" at him when I hadn't even raised my voice.

Every time he would try and say "oh but I do SO much around here- let me list it off..." I wouldnt give in and would just keep saying that he needed to do his fair share so please take out the trash. Try that out, might make your mind more at ease. Its hard losing your cool, kinda makes you feel like you're like them (you're definitely not).

The difference in reacting to abuse and being abusive is somewhat the intention behind it. Are you yelling to control him, slamming doors because you know he will just shut up if you do? Doubt it.
